set1.io: Objective k — Discuss imaging evaluation of neck masses and deep neck infections
set1.q: What are the three things contrast computed tomography of the neck evaluates in deep neck infection?
opts: A drainable abscess, airway compromise, and spread towards the mediastinum
Correct — the three questions this study is asked.
Cystic versus solid character, size, and vascularity
Those are the ultrasound descriptors for a neck mass.
Perineural spread, skull base involvement, and intracranial extension
Those are magnetic resonance strengths.
Bone erosion, gas, and foreign body
Those are general computed tomography findings, not this slide's three.

set1.io: Objective c — Interpret potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparations
set1.q: What concentration of potassium hydroxide does the deck's procedure specify?
opts: Forty per cent
Not the concentration given.
Twenty per cent
Correct — one drop of twenty per cent potassium hydroxide is added to the specimen.
Ten per cent
Ten per cent is a common alternative but is not the concentration in this procedure.
Five per cent
Not the concentration given.

set1.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set1.q: Which distinction does audiometry make?
opts: Unilateral from bilateral loss
Laterality is apparent clinically; the deck's stated distinction is the type of loss.
Conductive from sensorineural hearing loss
Correct — the type of loss, not merely its degree.
Effusion from perforation
That distinction is made by tympanometry with canal volume.
Acute from chronic otitis media with effusion
Audiometry does not date the disease.

set1.io: Objective c — Interpret potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparations
set1.q: During the potassium hydroxide procedure, how are the epithelial cells made visible?
opts: Increase the illumination and open the iris diaphragm fully
The procedure calls for reducing illumination, not increasing it.
Add a drop of methylene blue to the preparation
No counterstain is used in this procedure.
Warm the slide gently over a flame before reading
Warming is not one of the steps given.
Reduce the illumination by lowering the condenser
Correct — the step specified for the low-power examination.

set1.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set1.q: What does a punch biopsy provide, and what is it used for?
opts: A full-thickness sample, used only when melanoma is suspected
Excisional biopsy is preferred for suspected melanoma.
A superficial sample, used for raised epidermal lesions
That describes the shave biopsy.
A sample of the entire lesion, used for pigmented lesions of any size
Removing the entire lesion describes excisional biopsy.
A full-thickness sample, used for inflammatory rashes and small lesions
Correct — both halves as the slide gives them.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: Homonymous hemianopia is found. Where is the lesion, and what does the deck raise as a possible cause?
opts: Retrochiasmal, and it queries a stroke
Correct — the slide writes it with a question mark against stroke.
Chiasmal, and it queries a pituitary tumour
The pituitary lesion is the bitemporal pattern.
Prechiasmal, and it queries optic neuritis
A prechiasmal lesion causes monocular loss.
Retinal, and it queries a branch artery occlusion
The deck localises this pattern behind the chiasm.

set1.io: Objective h — Compare and contrast CT and MRI applications in head and neck pathology
set1.q: For which patients does the deck specifically favour computed tomography?
opts: Unstable or claustrophobic patients
Correct — both are named as reasons to choose computed tomography.
Pregnant patients and children
The deck does not name these here, and both are reasons to limit radiation.
Patients with implanted metal hardware
Not one of the reasons given on this slide.
Patients with impaired kidney function
Renal function is a contrast issue rather than a modality one here.

set1.io: Objective j — Identify common abnormalities of the orbit, sinuses, and neck on diagnostic imaging
set1.q: Which findings does orbital computed tomography show?
opts: Rim-enhancing fluid collection and necrotic lymph nodes
Those are the neck findings.
Cystic versus solid character, size and vascularity
Those are ultrasound descriptors for a neck mass.
Orbital cellulitis with fat stranding, abscess, blowout fracture and herniated orbital contents
Correct — the orbital column as listed.
Mucosal thickening, air-fluid levels and complete sinus opacification on the affected side
Those are the sinus findings.

set1.io: Objective i — Select appropriate imaging studies for common ophthalmologic and ENT disorders
set1.q: Which three presentations need no imaging at all?
opts: Otitis, neck mass, and simple soft-tissue infections
A neck mass is worked up beginning with ultrasound.
Uncomplicated otitis, deep neck infection, and simple abscesses
Deep neck infection requires contrast computed tomography of the neck.
Uncomplicated acute rhinosinusitis, otitis, and simple soft-tissue infections
Correct — the deck's no-imaging list.
Uncomplicated acute rhinosinusitis, orbital cellulitis, and simple soft-tissue infections
Orbital cellulitis is an emergency imaging indication.

set1.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set1.q: Which three indications for tympanometry does the deck list?
opts: Any ear pain, any ear discharge, and any hearing complaint
The list is more specific than this.
Suspected effusion, otitis media with effusion, and eustachian tube dysfunction
Correct — the three indications as given.
Suspected effusion, asymmetric hearing loss, and tinnitus
Asymmetric loss and tinnitus are not tympanometry indications here.
Persistent otitis media with effusion, hearing loss, and retrocochlear pathology
Those overlap with the audiometry list, not the tympanometry one.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: What does it mean if acuity does not correct with a pinhole, or worsens?
opts: The test should be repeated after instilling a topical anesthetic
Anesthetic belongs to the fluorescein examination.
Eye pathology is likely present
Correct — failure to correct points away from a simple refractive error.
The refractive error is greater than the pinhole can compensate for
The deck reads failure to correct as pathology, not as a larger refractive error.
The patient needs a near chart rather than a distance chart
Chart choice is not what the pinhole result indicates.

set1.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set1.q: What margin does the melanoma rule specify for the diagnostic biopsy?
opts: An excisional biopsy with no margin, cutting at the visible lesion edge
The rule specifies a narrow margin rather than none.
A narrow excisional biopsy with margins of one to three millimetres
Correct — narrow margins, because this biopsy is for diagnosis rather than cure.
A wide excisional biopsy with margins of one to two centimetres
Those are the definitive re-excision margins, taken after the diagnosis is made.
A narrow excisional biopsy with margins of one to three centimetres
The rule specifies millimetres for the diagnostic biopsy.

set1.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set1.q: What are the stated limitations of skin biopsy?
opts: Sampling error, and a delay of twenty-four to forty-eight hours for results
That delay belongs to throat culture, not to biopsy.
Operator skill and sampling technique
Those are the limitations of bedside microscopy.
Cost, and poor correlation with the clinical appearance
Neither is given as a limitation of biopsy here.
Sampling error, and procedural risks of bleeding, scarring and infection
Correct — both categories as listed.

set1.io: Objective k — Discuss imaging evaluation of neck masses and deep neck infections
set1.q: Which three characteristics does ultrasound establish when a neck mass is first worked up?
opts: Abscess versus phlegmon, airway patency, and mediastinal spread
Those are contrast computed tomography questions for deep neck infection.
Cystic versus solid, size, and vascularity
Correct — the three ultrasound answers listed.
Cystic versus solid, depth, and bone involvement
Depth and bone involvement are not what the deck assigns to ultrasound here.
Malignant versus benign, size, and nodal station
Ultrasound is not asked to make the malignancy call.

set1.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set1.q: How negative must middle-ear pressure be before it is considered significant for treatment?
opts: More negative than minus fifty millimetres of water
Fifty is the normal peak pressure point, not the treatment threshold.
More negative than minus one hundred millimetres of water
Not the figure given.
Any negative pressure at all
The notes set a specific threshold rather than treating any negativity as significant.
More negative than minus two hundred millimetres of water
Correct — the threshold given in the speaker notes.

set1.io: Objective l — Apply diagnostic test selection principles to common dermatologic, ophthalmologic, and otolaryngologic presentations
set1.q: Which four questions does the deck ask you to consider about any test?
opts: What does it cost, how long does it take, who performs it, and where is it available
Practical questions, but not the four the slide asks.
What is its sensitivity, what is its specificity, what is its predictive value, and what is its positive likelihood ratio
Those are Lecture 1 concepts, not this slide's four questions.
Is it invasive, is it painful, is it repeatable, and is it covered by insurance
None of these four is on the slide.
What does it evaluate well, when do we order it, what are its strengths and limitations, and how do the results confirm the condition
Correct — the four framing questions on the clinical applications slide.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: How is the visual field assessed at the bedside, and how is it assessed formally?
opts: Snellen testing at the bedside; formal perimetry by ophthalmology
Snellen measures acuity rather than field.
Confrontation fields at the bedside; formal perimetry or Amsler grid testing by ophthalmology
Correct — the bedside and the formal method as the slide pairs them.
Amsler grid at the bedside; confrontation fields by ophthalmology
The pairing is reversed.
Confrontation fields at the bedside; fluorescein examination performed by ophthalmology
Fluorescein assesses the cornea, not the field.

set1.io: Objective a — Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of common diagnostic tests used in dermatologic disorders
set1.q: A patient has a lesion you suspect is a neoplasm, or a rash that has not resolved. Which test does the deck's decision list point to?
opts: Point-of-care ultrasound
That branch is for distinguishing abscess from cellulitis.
Gram stain of a surface swab
A surface swab does not answer the neoplasm question.
Biopsy
Correct — neoplasm or a persistent rash routes to biopsy.
Potassium hydroxide preparation or culture
That branch is for a suspected infection.

set1.io: Objective e — Discuss the role of diagnostic testing in evaluation of soft tissue infections and abscesses
set1.q: Which ultrasound findings indicate an abscess?
opts: Dermal thickening with increased echogenicity and a cobblestone pattern
That is cellulitis.
A hyperechoic mass with posterior acoustic shadowing, sharply defined margins and no through-transmission
The deck describes enhancement behind an abscess, not shadowing.
Loss of the normal tissue planes with gas tracking along fascia
Gas is a computed tomography and magnetic resonance finding on this slide.
A hypoechoic or heterogeneous fluid collection, possibly with debris or septations, and posterior acoustic enhancement
Correct — the full description as given.

set1.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set1.q: Which lesion sites and sizes does the melanoma rule specifically include in its concession?
opts: Scalp, palmar and pigmented lesions
Only acral overlaps; scalp and pigmented generally are not named.
Truncal, nail unit and recurrent lesions
None of these three is named in the concession.
Facial, genital and ulcerated lesions
Genital and ulcerated lesions are not named here.
Facial, acral and very large lesions
Correct — the three the slide names.

set1.io: Objective i — Select appropriate imaging studies for common ophthalmologic and ENT disorders
set1.q: What is first-line for a neck mass, and what question does it answer?
opts: Ultrasound, distinguishing superficial or cystic from solid
Correct — the deck names lymphadenopathy and thyroid as the examples.
Contrast computed tomography, distinguishing abscess from phlegmon
That is the deep neck infection pathway.
Magnetic resonance imaging, distinguishing benign from malignant
Magnetic resonance follows ultrasound for specific reasons.
Fine needle aspiration, distinguishing reactive from neoplastic
The deck's imaging pathway begins with ultrasound.

set1.io: Objective h — Compare and contrast CT and MRI applications in head and neck pathology
set1.q: Which five strengths does the deck give magnetic resonance imaging?
opts: Soft-tissue contrast, speed, bone erosion, gas and oedema
Speed, bone erosion and gas are computed tomography advantages.
No ionizing radiation, cystic versus solid character, vascularity, size and the depth of a neck mass on ultrasound
The last three are what ultrasound contributes to a neck mass.
Superior soft-tissue contrast, no ionizing radiation, intracranial or orbital extension, perineural spread, skull base and tumours
Correct — the magnetic resonance list as given.
Speed, wide availability, bone detail, foreign bodies and acute trauma
Those are the computed tomography strengths.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: What does a healthy optic disc look like?
opts: A small central cup with a robust neuroretinal rim
Correct — the healthy disc as the slide describes it.
An enlarged, deeply excavated cup with an undermined rim
That is the glaucomatous disc.
A pale disc with sharply defined margins and no cup
Pallor without excavation suggests a different optic atrophy.
A cup filling more than two-thirds of the disc diameter
That is the glaucomatous ratio.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: Which two tonometers does the deck name for glaucoma screening?
opts: The Snellen tonometer and the Rosenbaum tonometer
Both are acuity charts, not tonometers.
The Schiotz indentation tonometer and the Goldman applanation tonometer
Correct — one indentation and one applanation instrument.
The Schiotz applanation tonometer and the Goldman indentation tonometer
The type is attached to the wrong name in each case.
The Tono-Pen and the Amsler tonometer
The Tono-Pen is named, but there is no Amsler tonometer.

set1.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set1.q: What is the limitation of throat culture?
opts: It cannot be performed in children
It is specifically recommended in children after a negative rapid test.
It requires a specialised transport medium not stocked in most clinics
The deck does not raise this.
Delayed results, taking twenty-four to forty-eight hours
Correct — the trade-off against the rapid antigen test's speed.
Sensitivity of only seventy to ninety per cent
That figure belongs to the rapid antigen test.

set1.io: Objective i — Select appropriate imaging studies for common ophthalmologic and ENT disorders
set1.q: Which study is indicated for complicated sinusitis or orbital cellulitis?
opts: Contrast computed tomography of the sinuses and orbits
Correct — the study named for this indication.
Contrast computed tomography of the neck
That is for deep neck infection.
Magnetic resonance imaging of the orbits with contrast
Magnetic resonance with contrast is named for acoustic neuroma and asymmetric sensorineural loss.
Ultrasound of the orbit
Ultrasound is offered for a neck mass, not for orbital cellulitis.

set1.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set1.q: What does the mnemonic VVEEPP stand for?
opts: Visual acuity, visual fields, external exam, extraocular movements, pupils, pressure
Correct — the six-step ophthalmic examination the deck opens with.
Vision, vessels, eyelids, extraocular movements, pupils, pressure
Vessels and eyelids are not the second and third items.
Visual acuity, visual fields, eyelids, external exam, pupils, photophobia
Photophobia is a symptom, not an examination step.
Visual acuity, vitreous, external exam, extraocular movements, papilloedema, pressure
Vitreous and papilloedema are findings rather than steps.

set1.io: Objective b — Describe indications for skin cultures and wound cultures
set1.q: How is the swab handled in the Levine method?
opts: Rotated for thirty seconds over the whole wound bed
The specified duration is five seconds over one to two centimetres.
Pressed onto the wound edge and held still for five seconds
The swab is rotated, not held still.
Rotated for five seconds over one to two centimetres of clean wound tissue, with enough pressure to express fluid
Correct — area, duration and pressure, all three as specified.
Rolled once across the entire width of the wound bed from edge to edge without applying pressure
The method requires rotation with pressure over a defined small area.

set1.io: Objective b — Describe indications for skin cultures and wound cultures
set1.q: Which sampling gives higher-yield results in complex wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers and pressure ulcers?
opts: Repeat superficial swabs taken on consecutive days
Repeating a superficial swab does not overcome its limitations.
Blood cultures drawn from two separate sites
Blood cultures are not offered for this purpose on this slide.
Deeper tissue biopsy or aspirate
Correct — higher yield than a superficial swab in complex wounds.
A superficial swab taken by the Levine method
The Levine method is an appropriate swab technique, but the deck still gives biopsy or aspirate the higher yield here.

set1.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set1.q: Which three indications for audiometry does the deck list?
opts: Suspected or confirmed hearing loss, persistent otitis media with effusion, and asymmetric loss
Correct — all three, with asymmetric loss serving to screen for retrocochlear pathology.
Suspected hearing loss, tinnitus, and vertigo
Tinnitus and vertigo are not on this list.
Eustachian tube dysfunction, middle-ear effusion, and tympanic membrane perforation
Those are the tympanometry indications.
Any ear pain, any ear discharge, and any foreign body
None of these three is listed for audiometry.

set2.io: Objective e — Discuss the role of diagnostic testing in evaluation of soft tissue infections and abscesses
set2.q: For what is computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging reserved in soft tissue infection?
opts: Deep-space infection, necrotizing infection, foreign body and gas
Correct — the four reasons listed to escalate beyond ultrasound.
Any abscess large enough to require drainage in theatre
Abscess size is not the criterion given.
Cellulitis that has failed forty-eight hours of oral antibiotics
Treatment failure is not the stated indication on this slide.
Any infection in an immunocompromised patient
Immunosuppression is a culture consideration here, not an imaging one.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: At what levels does screening pure tone audiometry present tones?
opts: Twenty-five to thirty decibels for adults, and fifteen to twenty decibels for children
Correct — the upper limits of normal hearing, set lower for children.
Fifteen to twenty decibels for adults, and twenty-five to thirty decibels for children
The two are the wrong way round.
Zero to ten decibels for adults, and ten to fifteen decibels for children
Neither figure matches the slide.
Forty to fifty decibels for adults, and thirty to forty decibels for children
Both figures are well above the levels given.

set2.io: Objective i — Select appropriate imaging studies for common ophthalmologic and ENT disorders
set2.q: Which study does the deck name for deep neck infection, and what does it say about ultrasound there?
opts: Magnetic resonance imaging of the neck, with ultrasound as a screening step
Magnetic resonance adds value for specific complications, not as first-line.
Plain radiography of the soft tissues of the neck, with ultrasound if negative
Plain films are not offered for this.
Contrast computed tomography of the neck, and it states that ultrasound is not helpful
Correct — the deck rules ultrasound out explicitly for this indication.
Ultrasound of the neck first, escalating to computed tomography if inconclusive
That sequence applies to a neck MASS, not to deep neck infection.

set2.io: Objective j — Identify common abnormalities of the orbit, sinuses, and neck on diagnostic imaging
set2.q: Which three computed tomography findings indicate sinus infection?
opts: Bone erosion, gas within soft tissue and perineural spread
Not the three the sinus column lists.
Mucosal thickening, air-fluid levels and sinus opacification
Correct — the three sinus findings listed.
Fat stranding, abscess and herniated orbital contents
Those are the orbital findings.
Rim-enhancing fluid collection and enlarged or necrotic lymph nodes
Those are the neck findings.

set2.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set2.q: What is the purpose of tonometry?
opts: To measure corneal thickness and evaluate for keratoconus
Corneal thickness affects the reading but is not what tonometry measures.
To assess the visual pathway and evaluate for field loss
That is visual field testing.
To assess corneal integrity and evaluate for abrasion
That is fluorescein examination.
To measure intraocular pressure and evaluate for glaucoma
Correct — both halves of the stated purpose.

set2.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set2.q: A patient has unilateral visual loss. Where does the deck localise this?
opts: To the optic chiasm
A chiasmal lesion produces bitemporal hemianopia rather than unilateral loss.
To a retrochiasmal lesion such as a stroke
That produces homonymous hemianopia.
To the optic nerve or the eye itself
Correct — unilateral loss is ocular or optic nerve.
To a systemic or intracranial cause
That is the reading for bilateral loss.

set2.io: Objective l — Apply diagnostic test selection principles to common dermatologic, ophthalmologic, and otolaryngologic presentations
set2.q: A contact-lens wearer presents with a painful red eye and foreign-body sensation. Which two bedside tests does this lecture point to?
opts: Visual acuity, then fluorescein examination under cobalt-blue light
Correct — acuity is indicated for every eye complaint, and this history is a fluorescein indication.
Tonometry, then visual field testing by confrontation
Tonometry is for suspected glaucoma; the field test assesses the pathway.
Fluorescein examination alone, since acuity will be reduced by the pain
Acuity is indicated for every eye complaint regardless.
Visual field testing, then contrast computed tomography of the orbits
Orbital imaging is reserved for proptosis, eye signs or neurologic signs.

set2.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set2.q: Which biopsy technique is preferred when melanoma is suspected?
opts: Incisional biopsy of the darkest quadrant of the lesion
The deck does not offer this as the preferred approach.
Excisional biopsy, which removes the entire lesion
Correct — the deck states excisional biopsy is preferred for suspected melanoma.
Punch biopsy, which gives a full-thickness sample
Punch is listed for inflammatory rashes and small lesions.
Shave biopsy, which samples raised epidermal lesions
A shave risks transecting the base and losing Breslow depth.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What is recorded on the vertical axis of an audiogram, and what does pure tone audiometry require of the room?
opts: Sound intensity on the vertical axis, and a quiet environment
Correct — both details from the same slide.
Frequency on the vertical axis, and a quiet environment
Intensity goes on the vertical axis.
Sound intensity on the vertical axis, and a soundproof booth in every case
The deck asks for a quiet environment rather than specifying a booth.
Compliance on the vertical axis, and a quiet environment
Compliance is the tympanogram's vertical axis, not the audiogram's.

set2.io: Objective k — Discuss imaging evaluation of neck masses and deep neck infections
set2.q: For which three complications does magnetic resonance add value in the neck?
opts: Cystic character, size, and vascularity
Those are ultrasound descriptors.
Bone erosion, gas, and foreign body
Those are computed tomography strengths.
Intracranial extension, vascular thrombosis, and osteomyelitis
Correct — the deck names Lemierre syndrome as the vascular thrombosis example.
Drainable abscess, airway compromise, and mediastinal spread
Those are the contrast computed tomography questions.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What is the sensitivity of the rapid streptococcal antigen test, and what does that produce?
opts: About fifty per cent, which makes the test unhelpful in practice
The figure given is higher, and the test is presented as useful.
About seventy to ninety per cent, which can lead to false negatives
Correct — imperfect sensitivity is why a negative result may need confirming.
About seventy to ninety per cent, which can lead to false positives
Limited sensitivity produces false negatives, not false positives.
About ninety-five to ninety-nine per cent, which makes confirmation unnecessary
The deck gives a lower figure and does require confirmation in children.

set2.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set2.q: Which Breslow depth corresponds to T2?
opts: One millimetre or less
That is T1.
More than two millimetres and up to four millimetres
That is T3.
More than four millimetres
That is T4.
More than one millimetre and up to two millimetres
Correct — T2 spans the interval above one and up to two millimetres.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What does a type AS tympanogram show, and what causes it?
opts: Negative middle-ear pressure with normal mobility, from eustachian tube dysfunction
That is type C.
Restricted mobility with a flat curve, from middle-ear effusion
That is type B.
Normal pressure with reduced mobility, from ossicular chain fixation or tympanosclerosis
Correct — the S stands for stiff or shallow.
Normal pressure with hypermobility, from ossicular disarticulation
That is type AD.

set2.io: Objective h — Compare and contrast CT and MRI applications in head and neck pathology
set2.q: Which five strengths does the deck give computed tomography?
opts: Superior soft-tissue contrast, no ionizing radiation, orbital extension, perineural spread, and skull base tumours
Those are the five magnetic resonance strengths.
Calcifications, sinuses, perineural spread, foreign bodies, and skull base disease
Perineural spread and skull base disease belong to magnetic resonance.
Bone, tumours, foreign bodies, vascular thrombosis, and osteomyelitis
The last three are given elsewhere as magnetic resonance contributions.
Calcifications and bone, sinuses, acute trauma and orbital fractures, foreign bodies, and unstable or claustrophobic patients
Correct — all five as listed.

set2.io: Objective i — Select appropriate imaging studies for common ophthalmologic and ENT disorders
set2.q: Which findings make sinus or orbital imaging an emergency?
opts: Facial swelling, proptosis, eye signs or neurologic signs
Correct — the four findings the deck flags as emergency imaging.
Fever, purulent discharge, facial pain and headache
These are ordinary sinusitis features and do not trigger emergency imaging.
Nasal obstruction, anosmia and postnasal drip
None of these is on the emergency list.
Hearing loss, tinnitus and vertigo
Those relate to the ear rather than the sinuses or orbit.

set2.io: Objective h — Compare and contrast CT and MRI applications in head and neck pathology
set2.q: What are the deck's two clinical pearls contrasting the modalities?
opts: Think computed tomography for tumours; think magnetic resonance for foreign bodies
Tumours go to magnetic resonance and foreign bodies to computed tomography.
Think computed tomography whenever iodinated contrast is contraindicated; think magnetic resonance whenever contrast is safe
Contrast status is not what the pearls turn on.
Think computed tomography for bone, trauma and speed; think magnetic resonance for soft tissue, nerves and tumour or intracranial extension
Correct — both pearls as the slide words them.
Think computed tomography for soft tissue and nerves; think magnetic resonance for bone and speed
The two pearls are swapped.

set2.io: Objective j — Identify common abnormalities of the orbit, sinuses, and neck on diagnostic imaging
set2.q: Which findings does neck computed tomography show?
opts: Dermal thickening, increased echogenicity and a cobblestoning pattern
Those are ultrasound findings in cellulitis.
Abscess as a rim-enhancing fluid collection, and enlarged or necrotic lymph nodes
Correct — the neck column, which extracts out of order from this three-column slide.
Fat stranding and herniated orbital contents
Those are orbital findings.
Air-fluid levels and sinus opacification
Those are sinus findings.

set2.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set2.q: Which lesions is a shave biopsy suited to?
opts: Any lesion where the entire lesion must be removed intact
That is the excisional biopsy.
Deep dermal nodules and lesions suspected of involving subcutaneous fat
A shave does not reach these; it is a superficial technique.
Raised epidermal lesions, basal and squamous cell carcinoma, and superficial rashes
Correct — the three uses given for shave biopsy.
Inflammatory rashes and small lesions where full thickness is needed
That is the punch biopsy.

set2.io: Objective c — Interpret potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparations
set2.q: What error does the deck warn about when a fungal infection is diagnosed clinically alone?
opts: Resistance develops to topical antifungals
Resistance is not raised on this slide.
Fungal infections can be misidentified
Correct — the slide's stated reason for confirming with microscopy.
Treatment is delayed while the culture is awaited
Delay is a limitation of culture, not of clinical-only diagnosis.
The wrong antifungal class is chosen
The slide does not make this claim.

set2.io: Objective b — Describe indications for skin cultures and wound cultures
set2.q: From which material must a Levine specimen not be taken?
opts: Exudate, eschar or necrotic material
Correct — all three are excluded because they reflect colonisation rather than infection.
Granulation tissue at the wound base
Clean wound tissue is exactly what should be sampled.
The wound edge where epithelium is advancing
Not excluded by the method.
Any area that has bled during cleaning
Bleeding is not an exclusion; pressure sufficient to express fluid is required.

set2.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set2.q: Which condition does the deck name as an ophthalmologic emergency indicating tonometry?
opts: Corneal ulcer
That is the urgent fluorescein finding.
Acute angle-closure glaucoma
Correct — named as an ophthalmologic emergency.
Chronic open-angle glaucoma
Open-angle disease is the one the deck says usually has normal pressure.
Orbital cellulitis
That is an imaging emergency on a later slide, not a tonometry indication.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What does a type C tympanogram indicate?
opts: Significant negative pressure in the middle ear cavity, from eustachian tube dysfunction
Correct — negative pressure with normal mobility.
Restricted tympanic membrane mobility, from middle-ear fluid or otitis media
That is type B.
Normal pressure with reduced mobility, from ossicular chain fixation
That is type AS.
Normal pressure with hypermobility, from ossicular disarticulation
That is type AD.

set2.io: Objective a — Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of common diagnostic tests used in dermatologic disorders
set2.q: How is most skin disease diagnosed?
opts: By skin biopsy, with history and inspection used to choose the biopsy site
Biopsy is reserved for specific indications, not routine diagnosis.
By culture, with history and inspection used to choose the transport medium
Culture is indicated for purulent lesions, not for skin disease generally.
By dermoscopy, with history and inspection used to confirm the reading
Dermoscopy is not presented as the routine diagnostic route in this lecture.
By history and visual inspection, with office testing added for uncertain diagnoses
Correct — testing supplements the clinical examination rather than replacing it.

set2.io: Objective d — Discuss indications for skin biopsy and common biopsy techniques
set2.q: To what depth must a melanoma biopsy extend, and why?
opts: Into the papillary dermis only, so the wound heals without a graft
Cosmetic healing is not the consideration the rule gives.
Deep enough to include the regional lymphatics, so nodal spread can be excluded
Nodal assessment is a separate procedure, not part of the biopsy depth rule.
Deep enough to avoid transecting the base, so Breslow depth can be measured
Correct — a transected base destroys the single most important prognostic measurement.
Deep enough to reach subcutaneous fat, so the Clark level can be assigned
The stated reason is Breslow depth, not Clark level.

set2.io: Objective b — Describe indications for skin cultures and wound cultures
set2.q: What are the limitations of superficial wound swabs?
opts: They require an antimicrobial-free cleaning step, and are uncomfortable for most patients
Neither is the limitation the slide names.
They are prone to contamination and colonisation, and may not correlate well with deep infection
Correct — both limitations as stated.
They are prone to contamination, and cannot provide susceptibilities
Susceptibilities are listed as an advantage of culture.
They take twenty-four to forty-eight hours, and are operator dependent
That delay is quoted for throat culture on a later slide.

set2.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set2.q: A patient's reduced acuity corrects with a pinhole. What does that indicate?
opts: Ocular pathology is likely present
That is indicated when acuity does not correct or worsens.
The optic nerve is likely involved
Nerve involvement would not correct with a pinhole.
The result is uninterpretable without formal refraction
The deck treats a pinhole correction as interpretable in itself.
A refractive error is the likely cause
Correct — correcting with a pinhole points to refraction rather than disease.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What are the axes of a tympanogram, and where does a normal pressure peak sit?
opts: Frequency along the horizontal axis and intensity along the vertical, with a normal peak at fifty decibels
Those are audiogram axes, not tympanogram ones.
Pressure along the horizontal axis and compliance along the vertical, with a normal peak at fifty millimetres of water
Correct — both axes and the normal peak point.
Compliance along the horizontal axis and pressure along the vertical, with a normal peak at fifty millimetres of water
The axes are the other way round.
Pressure along the horizontal axis and compliance along the vertical, with a normal peak at minus two hundred millimetres of water
Minus two hundred is the threshold at which negative pressure becomes significant for treatment.

set2.io: Objective a — Discuss indications, advantages, and limitations of common diagnostic tests used in dermatologic disorders
set2.q: Which three tests does the deck group together as bedside testing?
opts: Potassium hydroxide preparation, Tzanck smear and Gram stain
Correct — the three bedside tests on the slide.
Potassium hydroxide preparation, Wood lamp and Gram stain
The Wood lamp is not on this slide's bedside list.
Tzanck smear, Gram stain and skin culture
Culture is sent to the laboratory rather than performed at the bedside.
Potassium hydroxide preparation, Tzanck smear and dermoscopy
Dermoscopy is not one of the three named.

set2.io: Objective f — Describe indications and interpretation of visual acuity testing, fluorescein examination, tonometry and visual field testing
set2.q: What structural change does the deck's cross-sectional schematic of the glaucomatous disc show?
opts: Thickening of the retinal nerve fibre layer
The change is loss and collapse rather than thickening.
Detachment of the neurosensory retina
Retinal detachment is not what these panels show.
Swelling of the optic nerve head
Swelling describes papilloedema, not glaucomatous cupping.
Lamina cribrosa collapse
Correct — the schematic panel shows collapse of the lamina cribrosa.

set2.io: Objective g — Discuss indications for rapid streptococcal testing, throat cultures, audiometry and tympanometry
set2.q: What counts as a fail on primary-care conventional audiometry?
opts: More than ten decibels hearing level at one or more frequencies
Ten decibels is the air-bone gap figure, not the fail threshold.
More than forty decibels hearing level at two or more frequencies
Neither the level nor the number of frequencies matches.
Any threshold above zero decibels hearing level
That is not the criterion given.
More than twenty decibels hearing level at one or more frequencies
Correct — the threshold the deck sets for a fail.
